title: Home page redesign
summary: Built on the site's real code (fonts, colours, header, cards, copy). A player-first headline with one featured game. One filter bar where sort, players and genres each look different. Cards tinted by where the game runs, with a legend. Labelled header buttons. The creator pitch moves down the page.
why: Most visitors come to play, but the page opens with a pitch for creators, and nothing warns that the most popular games need a desktop app and your own disc. This puts a playable game first and shows where each game runs before anyone clicks.

title: Game page for emulator games
summary: Built on the site's real code. The player shows a three-step "Get ready to play" checklist with one button that names the next step. Game facts sit on one line under the title. Only Save, Share and … stay as buttons. Known issues fold into one line. The right rail becomes a plain "More like this" list.
why: On emulator games the setup steps sit below the fold and about ten equal buttons compete under the title, so new players hit a dead end and help questions pile up in the comments.
